premise_ledger.premise: cio_chunk_open hands the caller owned custody of a nullable chunk pointer
premise_ledger.note: Loaded into ResourceContracts but never reached at either corpus call site; probes O-A/O-D.

premise_ledger.premise: ctx, st, name, flags, size and err stay borrowed across cio_chunk_open
the chunk returned on success is ALSO linked into st->chunks, so the returned pointer is not sole custody
premise_ledger.note: In tension with R01's resource_return_owned; probe O-C shows the contract would report a discarded owned result at cio_scan.c:105.

premise_ledger.premise: cio_chunk_close releases the chunk (nonnull)
premise_ledger.note: Reaches 7 of 9 corpus call sites but always on an unresolved identity; 2 sites are inert (member-read receiver).

premise_ledger.premise: chunk_is_live at close
chunk_is_not_busy at close
chunk_has_no_task_or_route_custody at close (exclusivity)
close removes the stream link and the context link, releases name and object, decrements the counter
premise_ledger.note: Native leg: docs/reports/cycle19-native-teardown, cycle19-parent-teardown.

premise_ledger.premise: malloc yields a fresh owned nullable resource
premise_ledger.note: This contract does reach its call site: pp 2029 carries no diagnostic.

premise_ledger.premise: ch->name = strdup(name) is a fresh child allocation whose NULL result is never tested
premise_ledger.note: Native leg: cycle19-constructor-failures row 'Chunk name | Chunk succeeds with null name'.

premise_ledger.premise: the backend-failure arm unlinks _head then frees name then frees the object, exactly once each
premise_ledger.note: Checked only for injected arms at a harness caller: cycle19-constructor-failures (backend/data-buffer arms), cycle19-file-constructor-failures (arms 8-11). Statically: two indirect-access diagnostics plus unknown_alias `ch`.

premise_ledger.premise: free(NULL) is well defined, so a null ch->name does not make the rollback arm ill-formed
mk_list_add transfers containment into the stream list and conserves live resources
premise_ledger.note: contract/qcore declares mk_list_del and __mk_list_del but no mk_list_add anywhere.

premise_ledger.premise: mk_list_del releases no object and requires entry_is_live, exclusive_link_access, live reciprocal neighbours and entry distinct from neighbours
_state_head is linked only on the success exit, so the rollback arm's single mk_list_del is complete
cio_file_open publishes cf into ch->backend before all of its own failure arms, and those arms free cf without clearing ch->backend
premise_ledger.note: Only safe because cio_chunk.c:91 frees the parent on the same arm - a cross-function invariant no pass states.

premise_ledger.premise: cf->path custody moves into cf at cio_file.c:685; every failure arm frees path exactly once
premise_ledger.note: Archived diagnostics: unknown_alias `path` at pp 3267/3295/3303/3319/3326.

premise_ledger.premise: cio_memfs_open is the alternative child constructor selected by st->type
premise_ledger.note: Backend selection branch itself is unmodeled: two branch-condition diagnostics.

premise_ledger.premise: a SUCCESSFUL cio_chunk_open can return a chunk with fd == -1 and map == NULL (the resource-limit arm)
premise_ledger.note: This is why the caller runs cio_chunk_is_up / up_force / set_down at flb_input_chunk.c:2536-2543.

premise_ledger.premise: _cio_file_up returns CIO_ERROR with the descriptor still open when cio_file_update_size fails or when mmap_file returns CIO_ERROR
premise_ledger.note: cycle19-reopen-failures: 'Failed size lookup retains an unmapped descriptor'. Harness caller only.

premise_ledger.premise: on CIO_CORRUPTED or CIO_RETRY, _cio_file_up closes the descriptor it opened
the caller tests only ret == -1, so CIO_RETRY (-2) and CIO_CORRUPTED (-3) continue into the success path with set_down = FLB_TRUE
premise_ledger.note: The exit enumeration of flb_input_chunk_create is incomplete without this case.

premise_ledger.premise: cio_file_close unmaps, closes the descriptor, optionally deletes the backing file, then frees cf->path and cf
premise_ledger.note: Native leg: cycle19-file-close, cycle19-file-descriptor-failures. Two observed descriptor residuals after parent release under suppressed close are NOT release evidence.

premise_ledger.premise: cio_file_native_map stores MAP_FAILED (non-NULL) into cf->map when mmap fails
premise_ledger.note: cycle19-reopen-failures. Consequence: a later cio_file_down passes its `cf->map == NULL` guard at cio_file.c:927.

premise_ledger.premise: munmap_file releases the mapping and decrements the up counter only when cf->map != NULL and the unmap returns CIO_OK
premise_ledger.note: Native leg: cycle19-file-unmap-failures.

premise_ledger.premise: cio_chunk_down at flb_input_chunk.c:2602 releases exactly the descriptor and mapping the caller's own up_force acquired
premise_ledger.note: Depends on R19-R22 and R24.

premise_ledger.premise: the chunk counters require counter_is_live, exclusive_counter_access, c_unsigned_matches_usize, counter_in_range and counter_below_maximum
total_chunks is incremented only after backend success, so the rollback arm need not decrement
premise_ledger.note: cycle19-unsupported-constructors: 'the surviving tree has zero total and up chunk counters'.

premise_ledger.premise: flb_calloc yields a fresh owned nullable resource and flb_free releases it (nullable)
ic->chunk = chunk transfers chunk custody into the caller's own aggregate
premise_ledger.note: Pointer-field store: excluded by C02's non-pointer scalar whitelist. Probe O-G is Unknown; the same shape with an explicit resource_stored transfer (O-H) is Safe.

premise_ledger.premise: mk_list_add(&ic->_head, &in->chunks) publishes ic into the input instance's chunk list
msgpack_packer_init(&ic->mp_pck, ic, flb_input_chunk_write) installs a callback that retains ic
premise_ledger.note: Named callback blocker: unresolved callback custody edge, no reactor/callback record covers it.

premise_ledger.premise: flb_hash_table_add(..., ic, 0) publishes ic into a table with its own destructor policy
premise_ledger.note: Named alias blocker: four alternative container publications on the success exit.

premise_ledger.premise: flb_input_chunk_destroy discharges chunk, routes_mask and ic
premise_ledger.note: The declared cio_chunk_close contract is inert at 2797 because the receiver is a member read; probe O-E.

premise_ledger.premise: *err is a scalar out slot carrying no custody
premise_ledger.note: Archived: 'store through `*err` without an out-parameter contract' at pp 2048 and cio_file.c pp 3297/3305/3310/3328/3331.

premise_ledger.premise: the evidence-v2 chunk-lifecycle obligation inventory applies to this C source
premise_ledger.note: Derivation runs over a QCore frontend SourceProgram, not over the pinned C translation unit.

premise_ledger.note: Rejects with 'outside single borrowed chunk / int-or-void-result source profile'; both functions return pointers.

o04_recommendation.target: Per-arm constructor-to-caller cleanup discharge on the four early-return arms of flb_input_chunk_create (exits C2, C3, C4, C5).
o04_recommendation.property: On each of those arms the chunk identity produced at flb_input_chunk.c:2525 is released exactly once, by the cio_chunk_close on that arm, and no other tracked identity is released or left live.
explicitly_out_of_scope: the success exit C6 and its publications
the descriptor and mapping identities ID-D/ID-M
any claim about the declared cio_chunk_open contract's soundness

prerequisite_features.name: C02-P: direct pointer-field read admitted only as a Borrowed actual of a contracted call
prerequisite_features.why: without it the constructor call statement is rejected and `chunk` never binds (B01; probes O-A vs O-B)
prerequisite_features.depends_on: C02, extended - C02's whitelist excludes pointer-typed fields and any statement containing a call

prerequisite_features.name: array-declarator admission for `char name[64]`
prerequisite_features.why: flb_input_chunk.c:2514 is rejected by the same token gate (archived diagnostic at pp 19578)

prerequisite_features.name: borrowed declarations or W4 summaries for the intervening callees on the four arms
prerequisite_features.why: measured: O-F only reaches Safe once up_force and write_header carry borrowed contracts
prerequisite_features.caveat: cio_chunk_up_force is Borrowed only with respect to ID-P; it mutates ID-D and ID-M, so R19-R22 and R24 must be carried as named assumptions

prerequisite_features.name: per-exit disposition so an unmodeled success exit does not poison the four cleanup arms
prerequisite_features.why: the analyzer's published status is per function today; C6's publications (B08-B10) would otherwise force Unknown

card_dependencies.C02: necessary but not sufficient - its non-pointer scalar whitelist covers neither the constructor call's pointer-field actuals nor ic->chunk = chunk
card_dependencies.E-series: R19-R26 are bounded native observations at a harness caller only; O04 must import them as explicitly named assumptions, or wait for E-series to bind them to a production caller
card_dependencies.W4 (legacy_summary.rs): cannot contribute - no function on this path can pass its zero-diagnostic publication gate

o04_recommendation.precision_warning: Lifting the indirect-access gate on the constructor call also unmasks cio_scan_stream_files, which would then report a discarded owned result (probe O-C) and stay Unknown. All four archived 185-unit artifacts would change and must be re-pinned deliberately under hard invariants 3 and 5.

non_claims: No verdict is promoted. flb_input_chunk.c stays provisional Unsafe; cio_chunk.c, cio_scan.c and cio_file.c keep their archived statuses.
A provisional Unsafe is not an upstream defect claim, and none of the source observations here is one.
The declared contracts named as assumed are trusted declarations, not validated claims about the C bodies.
The native Cycle 19 observations cited are fixed injected runs at a harness caller; they do not establish production caller reachability, arbitrary OS failure behaviour or durability.
Nothing here establishes that any recommended feature is implementable at its stated boundary.
No CT mapping changes; coverage remains 11/50 mapped.
